method.basis: Static reading of supplied code contracts, intent comments, and test source/fixtures. No prior invariant suite or maintenance conclusion consulted.
method.validation: Not executed against either version. Version differences and suspected failures below are source-derived hypotheses, not validated results.

notation.state: Unprimed variables are pre-state; primed are post-state of the stated action. I/O/L/S are incoming voters, outgoing voters, active learners, staged learners. A is raft's acknowledged applied cursor; actual configuration application is a distinct event. P=pendingConfIndex, Q=uncommittedSize, M=normalized runtime quota (Config zero means unlimited).
notation.predicates: Clauses within each candidate are conjunctive under their stated scopes. 'Leads to' means eventual response under explicitly stated fairness, not a fixed time bound.
notation.leave: For well-formed supported messages, Leave(c) means a V2 zero change except optional Context: Transition=Auto and Changes empty. A V1 zero change converts to a one-operation V2 change, so is not Leave.
notation.cursor: Cursor(B)=last(B.CommittedEntries).Index if nonempty, else nonzero B.Snapshot.Metadata.Index, else 0.
notation.cost: cost(es)=sum(len(e.Data)); encoded entry size, Index and Term are not payload cost. Assume arithmetic without uint64 overflow.
notation.retained: Retained entries belong to the current log identity. Retransmission is not another append; legitimate truncation/replacement is recorded. No global one-configuration-entry rule is imposed on bootstrap or historical logs.
notation.observation: Use actual pre/input/post observations and the source-backed history named per candidate. Monitors must not synthesize missed Advance crossings, conflate ApplyConfChange with Advance, or discard counterexamples by copying an implementation guard into an obligation.
notation.environment: Correct callers obey persistence and ordered application contracts. Node's documented deferred application after Advance is permitted, with completion ordered before later committed batches. Network may delay, drop, or duplicate messages. Liveness separately assumes eventual service/delivery as stated.

scope_exclusions: No generic Raft safety inventory: leader uniqueness, unrelated log matching, reads, storage contracts, and similar obligations are excluded.
README edits, diagnostics/string parsing, test plumbing, equivalent refactoring, and cosmetic test fixes yield no additional core protocol candidate.
Sorted campaign generation is checked for recipient preservation, not network order: the supplied vocabulary has a message multiset.
Exact Next=LastIndex is a probing strategy, not elevated into a universal requirement. Dormant empty bootstrap Next=Match=0 is permitted.
No mixed-version wire compatibility guarantee is inferred. Old/new interactions refer to changed behavior interacting with retained contracts and paths.

core_candidates.title: Configuration admission uses the semantic joint phase
core_candidates.scope: Well-formed V1/V2 proposals at a healthy member leader, without a transfer or pending barrier, with sufficient quota; operations are otherwise valid.
predicate: Let c=Decode(entry).AsV2(), J=(O nonempty), and PhaseOK=(J AND Leave(c)) OR (NOT J AND NOT Leave(c)). In a locally appended proposal batch, each unblocked configuration slot retains its original kind and payload iff PhaseOK; phase-refused slots become empty EntryNormal, do not change configuration, and do not reserve a new pending configuration index.

Empty Changes with JointImplicit or JointExplicit is an ENTER request: permit it in a nonempty stable configuration and refuse it in an already joint configuration. Absence of operations alone is not a sufficient leave predicate.
A context-only V2 leave remains legal in joint state. A V1 zero-ID operation remains a non-leave operation, even though its application is a membership no-op.

examples.pre: I={1,2}, O={1}, P=A=4; quota available.
examples.forbidden: Append a configuration entry which later attempts to enter joint again and fails.
examples.allowed_control: Propose V2{Context:'manual'}; preserve its payload and leave when that committed entry is applied.

examples.pre: I={1}, O=empty, P=A=4.
examples.forbidden: Convert a valid request to enter {1}&&{1} to a normal no-op solely because Changes is empty.
examples.allowed_control: Retain it; application enters {1}&&{1}, AutoLeave=true. A true context-only leave in the same stable state is instead refused as a normal no-op.

evidence.basis: Explicit modes use joint consensus; leaving uses only optional Context.
V1 conversion and EnterJoint/LeaveJoint distinguish transition mode from an empty operation list.
Entering an unchanged joint configuration is allowed; entering twice is rejected.
Nested membership changes and leave outside joint become normal no-ops.
New wantsLeaveJoint uses len(Changes)==0, weaker than LeaveJoint().

core_candidates.old_new_interaction: Old admission checked only pending status. New phase checks add rejection behavior but appear to misclassify empty explicit/implicit enter requests. Preserve the API meaning rather than redefining leave to fit the guard.
limits: Malformed protobufs, unknown enums, and independently invalid membership operations are outside scope.

core_candidates.title: Pending configuration serialization includes automatic exits
core_candidates.scope: Leader-local configuration appends after bootstrap, including external requests and automatic exits.
predicate: In leader states, P >= max({index(e): retained configuration entry e has index(e)>A} union {0}). P may conservatively exceed the exact last configuration index and need not point at a configuration entry.

A local configuration append at k requires no earlier retained configuration entry with index>A at the instant of append. Within a proposal batch, once one slot reserves a configuration index, later configuration slots become empty normal entries.

Appending an automatic exit at k must make P cover k; the updated test specifies P=k. Neither a manual nor automatic competing exit may be appended while k>A. Refused slots do not replace that reservation.

For one joint episode in an unchanged retained log, at most one exit entry may be retained before actual ApplyConfChange of that exit closes the episode. Advance passing the exit index does not by itself close the episode or authorize another exit. Retransmission of the same entry, or replacement after legitimate truncation, is not a second exit.

examples.pre: Entry 4 installed a joint AutoLeave configuration; A becomes 4; automatic exit is appended at 5.
examples.action: Before applying 5, propose another leave or Advance a batch that does not apply 5.
examples.forbidden: Leave P=4 or append a second exit at 6 while 5 is pending.
examples.allowed_control: Set P=5; a competing request becomes empty EntryNormal. Ordinary proposals remain possible.

examples.pre: New leader inherits a normal entry 8, with A=7.
examples.forbidden: Demand that P identify an actual configuration entry, excluding a conservative normal-tail barrier.
examples.allowed_control: P=8 is allowed until the inherited prefix is acknowledged; equality with the last actual configuration entry is not required.

examples.pre: AutoLeave episode entered at 4; exit 5 already retained; caller has not yet applied exit 5.
examples.action: Use deferred application and Advance the Ready through exit 5 before calling ApplyConfChange(5).
examples.forbidden: Append a second exit 6 just because A crossed P=5 while the installed configuration still has AutoLeave=true.
examples.allowed_control: Keep the existing exit as the episode's sole exit, then close the episode when ApplyConfChange(5) actually runs.

evidence.basis: One unapplied configuration; new leaders conservatively reserve the inherited tail.
Leader must be certain no previous configuration remains unapplied.
Second configuration becomes no-op without changing P; inherited normal entries may set P.
Automatic exit advances pendingConfIndex to the new unstable entry.
Successful automatic append did not update pendingConfIndex.

core_candidates.old_new_interaction: Groups external serialization, auto-exit reservation, and duplicate suppression. New tracking addresses an old gap that checking only external proposals would miss.
limits: Do not impose a blanket one-configuration-entry rule on bootstrap or inherited historical logs.

core_candidates.title: Automatic exit remains an obligation across application and leadership changes
core_candidates.support: API promise and tests; alternate schedules derived from API
core_candidates.scope: An applied or restored joint AutoLeave configuration; a healthy stable leader remains a voter.
predicate: Track joint episode e and its establishing entry/snapshot index j, actual configuration installation, and inherited-tail barrier b recorded at current leader election (or j when this leader enters e). These are history facts, not aliases of mutable P.

Eligible(e) means current installed configuration is e with O nonempty and AutoLeave, local node is leader in I union O, A>=max(j,b), and no retained exit for e exists and no earlier retained configuration with index>A remains. A retained exit still discharges the proposal obligation when A passed its index but its actual application is deferred.

On the normal path, Advance(B) acknowledging the entering entry after ApplyConfChange installed it must append one semantic leave in the same call when no exit is already retained. It must not fail/panic because of quota. New behavior uses empty Data and zero payload cost.

More generally, with a stable eligible leader, fair local ticks/Ready service, and eventual completion of deferred application, Eligible(e) leads to an exit proposal even when A already reached j before AutoLeave was installed or before leadership began. With available joint quorums, eventual message delivery, persistence, and ordered application, that exit is eventually applied and O becomes empty and AutoLeave=false. No new client proposal is assumed.

Automatic exit generation requires an installed joint AutoLeave configuration and a leader. Explicit/manual joint configurations are not auto-left. HardState.Commit beyond j alone is not acknowledgement of applying j.

examples.pre: I={1,2},O={1},AutoLeave=true restored at 4; new leader starts with A=lastIndex=4, b=4.
examples.action: Commit and Advance its new leader normal entry 5, then continue fair processing.
examples.forbidden: Remain joint forever because oldApplied

examples.forbidden: Install AutoLeave after the only cursor crossing and permanently strand the exit obligation.

examples.forbidden: Reject, panic, or indefinitely postpone the exit because of quota.
examples.allowed_control: Append the zero-payload exit. In an otherwise identical AutoLeave=false episode, append no automatic exit.

evidence.basis: Implicit transitions/AutoLeave promise automatic exit when safe; explicit transitions wait for the application.
Advance can precede completion of application; ApplyConfChange is a separate action.
Advance initiates auto-exit; new strict cursor crossing interacts with inherited barrier.

Implicit exit versus explicit context-bearing manual exit.

core_candidates.title: Configuration effects occur at application and preserve the requested transition
core_candidates.scope: Accepted simple, explicit/implicit joint, and exit entries; valid bootstrap/restoration are separate installation events.
predicate: Propose, append, commit, Ready capture, and Advance alone do not apply a configuration entry. Outside bootstrap/restoration, membership changes through ordered ApplyConfChange for committed entries.

V1 single operations and one-operation V2 Auto use the simple result with O empty and AutoLeave=false. Non-leave V2 Auto with multiple operations, or JointImplicit/JointExplicit, sets O to former I, applies operations to incoming membership, and sets AutoLeave iff Auto or JointImplicit.

Applying a semantic leave to (I,O,L,S,AutoLeave), O nonempty, yields (I,empty,L union S,empty,false). Staged learners become IsLearner=true; outgoing-only voters with no remaining membership lose Progress; retained peers preserve their replication evidence.

Entering application, exit generation/commitment, and exit application are distinct. Both voter halves remain active until exit application. Returned ConfState equals installed membership/AutoLeave and is the configuration recorded in subsequent snapshots.

examples.pre: Committed entry 4 adds node 2 with JointExplicit; current configuration {1}; A=3.
examples.forbidden: Activate new members on proposal, skip joint state, or automatically exit Explicit.
examples.allowed_control: Before Apply retain {1}; at Apply install {1,2}&&{1},AutoLeave=false; remain until committed manual leave is applied.

examples.pre: I={2},O={1},L={3},S={1},AutoLeave=true; exit 5 is appended.
examples.forbidden: Demote 1 to active learner and drop outgoing quorum merely on append/commit.
examples.allowed_control: Keep 1 an outgoing voter until Apply(5); then I={2},L={1,3},O=S=empty,AutoLeave=false.

evidence.basis: Configuration active on application, not append; two-stage joint transition.
V1/V2 simple equivalence, transition modes, bytes/context preservation, staged learners, returned ConfState.
Entering preserves outgoing majority; leaving activates staged learners.
Apply committed configurations and record returned state in snapshots.

history: ordered configuration application events separately from Advance

core_candidates.title: Ready acknowledgement covers only its captured batch and preserves new work
core_candidates.scope: Configuration application emits replication messages or Advance creates an automatic exit while an earlier Ready is being handled.
predicate: For valid Advance(B), A'=Cursor(B) when Cursor(B)>0, else A'=A. B.HardState.Commit is not a substitute for the committed page cursor.

Advance(B) acknowledges persistence only of the matching entries/snapshot captured in B and saved by the caller. An exit created during Advance and absent from B.Entries remains outstanding for persistence/publication in later Ready.

Messages created after B acceptance by ApplyConfChange, and entries created during Advance(B), cannot be consumed as part of B merely because they are in live state. Still-valid effects remain queued until captured in a subsequent accepted Ready, and fresh entries remain outstanding until correctly stabilized. A queued new message or unstabilized new entry makes RawNode.HasReady true; Node may withhold the next delivery until the current Advance.

Under fair Ready service without intervening supersession, the next accepted batch carries these effects. Captured entry/HardState persistence precedes publication of dependent messages under the caller contract.

examples.pre: Accepted B ends at entering entry 4; ApplyConfChange generates probes to new nodes.
examples.forbidden: Mark 5 stable using B, discard new probes, or report no work until another client request.
examples.allowed_control: Keep exit 5 unstable and probes pending; expose both in following Ready while caller storage still ends at 4.

examples.pre: B.HardState.Commit=8, but paginated B.CommittedEntries ends at 4.
examples.forbidden: Set A=8, clear a barrier at 6, or consume entries 5-8 as if delivered.
examples.allowed_control: Set A=4 and retain remaining application work/barriers.

evidence.basis: Point-in-time Ready, captured entries/page, distinct acknowledgement.
AcceptReady clears captured messages; HasReady observes new work; Advance takes captured batch.
Respect pagination; stabilize only captured entries/snapshot.
Auto-exit not yet in storage belongs to next Ready.
Second Ready carries exit and probes.
Committed entries delivered in separate pages.

core_candidates.title: Zero payload bypasses quota without disabling ordinary backpressure
core_candidates.support: explicit new intent and test; retained ordinary contract
core_candidates.scope: Local append admission after role, transfer, and phase checks; finite normalized quota M.
predicate: cost(es)=sum(len(e.Data)); entry type tags, Index, Term, and protobuf framing are not payload charges.
Otherwise admissible zero-payload batches are quota-accepted for every Q, including Q>M, and leave Q unchanged. Includes an empty normal entry and internally generated nil-Data V2 exit.

For ordinary positive-payload batch cost s, quotaAccept iff Q=0 OR Q+s<=M. Acceptance gives Q'=Q+s; quota rejection leaves log and Q unchanged and returns ErrProposalDropped at the local proposal interface.
The first oversized batch is allowed when Q=0; Q<=M is not a state invariant. This does not settle positive-size configuration exemption (U01).

examples.pre: M=8,Q=16 after an allowed oversized first proposal.
examples.action: Append an otherwise admissible empty normal entry or nil-Data automatic exit.
examples.forbidden: Reject because Q>M, charge framing bytes, or panic during auto-exit.
examples.allowed_control: Accept with Q=16. An ordinary one-byte entry in the same state is dropped.

examples.forbidden: Enforce an absolute maximum by rejecting the first oversized batch.
examples.allowed_control: Accept with Q=16; reject a subsequent positive payload until quota is released.

evidence.basis: Uncommitted quota and explicit zero-payload exception.
PayloadSize=len(Data), independent of Index/Term.
Positive limit, first oversized batch, empty entry accepted while over limit.
Quota guard lacked s>0 exemption.

core_candidates.old_new_interaction: Allows intended new empty-entry behavior and old oversized-first behavior, while forbidding an overbroad relaxation admitting arbitrary positive payload.
limits: Config limit 0 is normalized to unlimited. Numeric overflow is outside this abstraction.

core_candidates.title: Advance releases its own payload accounting, with saturation
core_candidates.scope: Moved reduceUncommittedSize call in Advance, automatic appends, and inherited entries.
predicate: For Advance(B) without a reset, let d=cost(B.CommittedEntries), s=cost(entries freshly appended during that Advance). Q'=max(0,Q-d)+s: reduction precedes charging fresh appends. In the new automatic-exit path s=0.
Do not subtract B.Entries, all entries up to live committed, a HardState.Commit delta, or a snapshot index. Release the acknowledged committed page only.
Saturate at zero because inherited/previous-term entries may not have been charged. Do not equate Q to all bytes currently above committed: the estimate resets and releases wait for Advance.

examples.pre: Q=12; B.Entries has 20 payload bytes, B.CommittedEntries has 4; HardState.Commit exceeds that page.
examples.forbidden: Set Q=0 by subtracting all persisted/committed bytes, or forget release and leave Q=12.
examples.allowed_control: Set Q=8.

examples.pre: Q=3; acknowledged committed page includes 7 inherited payload bytes.
examples.forbidden: Unsigned underflow or a negative debt that blocks later proposals.
examples.allowed_control: Saturate Q=0; next positive proposal can use the empty-quota exception.

evidence.basis: Estimate resets; Advance releases committed entries; reduction saturates.
Releasing committed payload returns accounting to zero.
Reduction followed potential auto-append.

core_candidates.title: A new peer is probed without inventing replication knowledge
core_candidates.scope: New Progress allocation by configuration addition/restore; distinct from becomeLeader reset.
predicate: At creation of a genuinely new peer p with local last index N, before optional sending: Match=0, mode=Probe, inflights empty, RecentActive=true, IsLearner reflects active learner membership, not staged LearnersNext.

For N>0, a valid initial probe cursor is 1<=Next<=N+1. For N=0, dormant Next=0 is allowed by new fixtures, as is former Next=1. Neither implies acknowledged storage; no underflowed predecessor may be published.

An idempotent addition or promotion/demotion of an existing peer preserves Match and replication evidence instead of reinitializing it. Optional sends may subsequently change Next/mode/paused/inflights under send contracts.
At the API boundary a fresh peer still has Match=0 and cannot be Replicate without acknowledgement. A snapshot send may have moved it to Snapshot, or its first probe may already have paused it.

core_candidates.title: Adding a peer starts catch-up without a fresh client proposal
core_candidates.support: new intent and tests; snapshot-only boundary is derived
core_candidates.scope: ApplyConfChange on a leader remaining a voter, adding absent p with lastIndex>0; storage supplies a usable log probe or suitable nonempty snapshot; fresh peer is unpaused.
predicate: By completion of the configuration switch, p has an outgoing valid catch-up attempt: MsgApp probe containing retained entries, or MsgSnap when needed history is compacted and a suitable snapshot is available. The obligation does not depend on committed advancing.
A probe uses a locally known predecessor index/term and contiguous retained entries. It does not certify that the recipient matches the predecessor; rejection by an empty peer is allowed.

With eventual delivery/replies, local processing, available storage, and stable leadership/membership, that empty peer eventually catches up via log or snapshot. Rejection of the initial probe cannot permanently strand it.
No immediate acknowledgement or empty-message broadcast to caught-up peers is required. Temporary snapshot unavailability and paused existing peers permit deferral.

core_candidates.title: Reconfiguration uses the installed quorum and communicates enabled commits
core_candidates.scope: Commit decisions in and after changed switchToConfig, including joint additions and removed-leader tail completion.
predicate: For installed C, q(C) is the largest index acknowledged through Match by a strict majority of I and, if O nonempty, a strict majority of O. Learners and absent nodes add no vote; the leader is not an implicit extra voter.

On a surviving-voter leader switch: if q(C)>committed and term(q(C))=currentTerm, committed'=q(C), otherwise committed'=committed. Enlarging membership never uncommits the existing prefix even when q(C) becomes smaller.

When the switch advances committed, each non-self unpaused peer for which a log append can be formed gets a newly emitted MsgApp with Commit=committed', even with no entries. Paused/snapshot-needed peers retain ordinary send constraints.
Later commit advancement for retained pre-change entries uses current C even if a removed node temporarily retains Leader role. The joint exit itself needs both voter halves until it is applied.

core_candidates.title: Leadership transfer follows voter membership through staged demotion
core_candidates.scope: Active transfer during configuration switch on a leader that remains a voter; subsequent transfer requests and TimeoutNow generation.
predicate: Let V'=I' union O'. If old target t!=0 and t is absent from V', the switch must clear transferTarget even when Progress[t] remains as a learner.

core_candidates.title: Campaign and voting respect observer-local configuration during promotion lag
core_candidates.support: new regression trace and existing intent
core_candidates.scope: Sorted campaign generation and a promoted voter that still locally believes it is a learner.
predicate: For a campaign needing remote votes, newly generated request recipient multiset is exactly one per member of candidate I union O except self. Active learners absent from that union are not solicited/counted. Sorting changes order, not membership.

On a valid higher-term MsgVote with CheckQuorum lease suppression disabled and up-to-date candidate log, a locally marked learner must grant the vote: higher-term processing clears an old vote, response uses request term without rejection, and the receiver records the candidate vote. Local learner status is not a veto.

The candidate counts that response when sender belongs to its own installed voter configuration, even if sender lacks the promotion entry. Conversely, a locally active learner cannot initiate its own campaign; normal eligibility/log/vote rules remain.

core_candidates.title: A removed leader cannot accept new work or obstruct replacement forever
core_candidates.support: safety tested; progress intent explicitly identified as unfixed
core_candidates.scope: Applied final membership excludes leader from all voters and learners; current voters remain healthy and connected.
predicate: After removal is installed locally, new local MsgProp cannot append entries. Drop/error behavior at the appropriate API boundary is allowed. Entries accepted before removal may still complete under the new quorum (C10).

For stable final configuration excluding n, if a current quorum has applied it, ticks/caller/network processing are fair, and no re-addition occurs, RemovedLeader(n) leads to role(n)!=Leader OR cessation of n's continuing leader-maintenance messages that suppress current voters' elections.

Do not require synchronous role!=Leader in the exact ApplyConfChange post-state, a prescribed term change, successor, or immediate TimeoutNow. Transient removed leadership completing old work is allowed; indefinite heartbeat suppression is forbidden.

examples.forbidden: Append baz or count 1 to commit bar.

examples.allowed_control: 1 relinquishes or stops suppressing elections. A bounded interval of finishing already accepted work is permitted.

limits: Liveness is intent-backed, not a passing test assertion. Exact handover latency/method is unresolved in U03.

core_candidates.title: Simple changes report validation failure without partial installation
core_candidates.support: directly changed validation path and tests
core_candidates.scope: confchange.Changer.Simple, including removed redundant block that swallowed an error; distinct from raft.ApplyConfChange panic policy.
predicate: Compatible(C,prs) means every ID in I union O union L union S has Progress; S subset O and staged peers IsLearner=false; L disjoint from I union O and active learners IsLearner=true; O empty implies S empty and AutoLeave=false.

Successful Simple(ops) returns nonempty I', empty O', Compatible(C',prs'), and |I symmetric_difference I'|<=1. Failure of input compatibility, operation validity, nonempty-voter, nonjoint-input, or result compatibility validation returns a non-nil error; never (zero configuration, zero progress, nil error).

Original tracker configuration and Progress membership/learner fields remain unchanged by the helper on success and failure; caller installs only a successful result. Zero-ID operations are ignored. First voter addition to a valid empty bootstrap input is allowed.
